decisive_moments.reason: Con directly identified the central unresolved premise: a local component may not reliably recognize when it is outmatched, especially in high-stakes or accessibility contexts. This attacks the operational feasibility of pro's proposed guarded architecture rather than merely disputing its benefits.

Con clarified that the debate is about the default under a stipulated substantial capability gap. It showed that local-first creates hardware, maintenance, compatibility, and exclusion costs, while cloud-first can be mitigated through abstraction, regional processing, retention limits, encryption, and spending controls.

Pro effectively framed long-term privacy, replaceability, offline availability, and vendor dependence as production concerns, and appropriately conceded that local-first cannot mean local-only. However, it did not establish that consent-based escalation is safe when the local system cannot detect its own limitations.

flags.quote: cloud-first makes disclosure, recurring payment, availability, and policy dependence the baseline, often before users can meaningfully choose
A local-first system can refuse, defer, or request consent for stronger cloud assistance
